# Sutra Full Audit
## Executive Summary
Sutra is a local-first, static-hosted student/life/work workspace — a single-page web app with **no required backend, no telemetry, optional E2E-encrypted multi-device sync, and an optional in-product AI assistant**. It is built on a strict no-build philosophy: classic <script> tags, global-scope IIFEs, no bundler, no TypeScript, no test framework beyond node:test and Playwright. The codebase is ~290,000 lines of code (196k JS, 69k CSS, 22k HTML), concentrated in a single **85,392-line src/core/app.js** monolith that owns routing, persistence, theming, the Notes editor, the Timeline, ~12 per-view renderers, encrypted backup, Drive sync, the Sutra Cloud sync bridge, the assistant chat plumbing, the modal manager, the toast manager, the tutorial positioning, the chatbot FAB, the onboarding flow, and dozens of normalization helpers.
The product's strongest layers — sync, persistence, the assistant safety boundary, the action system, the encrypted-backup envelope, the Supabase RLS posture, the service worker, the test suite for sync — are **genuinely excellent** engineering. They would be impressive inside a funded Series-A company, let alone a single maintainer's project. The protocol-aware, AAD-bound, deterministic three-way merge with conflict-storm circuit breaker, lamport-based dedup, and verified-wipe semantics is the kind of work most "local-first" projects aspire to and few deliver.
The product's weakest layers — visual consistency, the CSS system, the 85k-line monolith, the modal/scroll-lock architecture, the absence of inert on background content, the ratchet-as-guardrail pattern, and the source-text-regex unit tests — are **the predictable debt of organic growth**. The team wrote a June 2026 internal UI_UX_POLISH_AUDIT (docs/audits/UI_UX_POLISH_AUDIT_2026-06.md) that already identifies most of these issues, and the issues remain unfixed two months later — evidence that the consistency debt is known-but-backlogged rather than unknown.
Rough ratings (1–10, with reasoning):
- **Engineering / Codebase:** 5/10. Excellent subsystems, but the 85k-line app.js monolith with 391 innerHTML writes, 774 addEventListener calls, 31 window.Sutra* exports, and 142 console.warn/catch swallow points is a structural drag that no individual change can fix.
- **Architecture:** 6/10. Strong module boundaries on sync/persistence/assistant/dom-safety; collapsed boundary between app.js and almost every UI feature; legacy/compat layers retained past their useful life.
- **Reliability:** 8/10. The persistence/sync failure-mode coverage is excellent — readback verification, conditional writes, conflict detection, conflict-storm breaker, snapshot-required trip. Real holes: cross-tab races without Web Locks; legacy migration promise that never resolves; verifyDatabasesGone lying on Firefox/Safari.
- **Maintainability:** 4/10. app.js is genuinely unreviewable. Custom inline-handler binding, parallel style systems, source-text-regex tests, and a 4.5 MB / 80k-line **size floor** in core-runtime-integrity.mjs actively prevent extraction. The AGENTS.md "landmines" section itself names 16 separate categories of cross-cutting landmines.
- **UI:** 5/10. Strong visual styling per individual surface; weak visual consistency across surfaces. 26 themes, 47 CSS files, 936 !important declarations in styles.css alone, two parallel token systems that don't talk to each other.
- **UX:** 6/10. The product feels cohesive at the surface — calm language, single primary nav, signature themes — but the 14 primary views plus hidden tabs, two parallel navigation taxonomies (top-row More + mobile More sheet), and 264 inline onclick= handlers betray accumulated surface friction.
- **Performance:** 6/10. No virtual DOM, no Suspense, no skeleton states. SutraModalManager observes document.documentElement and scans 25 selectors on every qualifying mutation (mitigated by rAF coalescing). 391 innerHTML writes means many views do full template renders. Bench is reasonable (<20s cold start, <60s encrypted export) but the heavy-workspace bench is the only perf signal — there is no production telemetry or regression baseline.
- **Testing:** 6/10. Strong in depth where it counts (sync crypto/merge/engine, action system, DOM safety, envelope tamper matrix, real-Supabase certification). Weak in breadth: no coverage tooling, no real property fuzzing, ~8 source-text-regex "contract" tests that masquerade as behavior tests, and a chaos-persistence.spec.mjs that asserts only "the page rendered something."
- **Security / Privacy Engineering:** 7/10. Defense-in-depth is genuinely thoughtful: prompt-injection fences, action-system schema validation, target-snapshot freshness, AAD-bound AES-GCM, RLS with anchored regex, security-definer RPCs, search_path pinning, deny-by-default vault key CAS. Real holes: 'unsafe-inline' in script-src amplifies any DOM-sink bug; the workspace lock is a UX gate, not encryption-at-rest (acknowledged in code but the UI affordance is stronger than the protection); the credential vault's per-profile key is decryptable by any same-origin script with no passphrase prompt.
- **Overall Product Coherence:** 6/10. As a product it feels coherent — local-first, student-focused, calm visual identity. As a codebase it feels like five products glued together. The "Sutra Cloud", "Sutra Intelligence", "Student OS upgrade", and "Today Redesign" feature waves (docs/FEATURE_WAVE_PROGRESS.md) each added their own vocabulary and the consolidation never happened.
## What Is GOOD
### 1. The sync subsystem is exemplary (preserve as-is)
src/sync/sync-protocol.js (348 LOC), sync-merge.js (1,047 LOC), sync-engine.js (659 LOC), sync-crypto.js (354 LOC), sync-transport.js (581 LOC), sync-store.js (421 LOC), plus supabase/sync-schema.sql (794 LOC). This is a real, working E2E-encrypted multi-device sync with: lamport-based opIds, deterministic three-way recursive merge with HTML block-level LCS, tombstone retention, conflict-storm circuit breaker (8 novel conflicts / 60s window), snapshot bootstrap when stale, stale-cursor retry bounded at 3, account-scoped IDB prefixes, security definer RPCs with set search_path = pg_catalog, public, deny-direct RLS with anchored regex ^<uid>/[0-9a-f]{64}$, vault-key CAS preventing split-brain, advisory locks per user on push, sync_authorize_device binding the JWT session_id to a device row, and a deliberate wipe-instruction verifier (validateVerifiedWipeInstruction) that never trusts a generic 401/403 as a wipe signal. The unit-test suite (sync-engine.test.mjs 806 LOC, sync-merge.test.mjs 571 LOC, sync-crypto.test.mjs 224 LOC, sync-store.test.mjs 294 LOC, sync-schema.test.mjs 184 LOC) verifies real behavior — three-device convergence, tombstone replay, tampered-envelope rejection, AAD-bound relabel detection, conflict-store-failure aborts before apply/push/baseline-advance. This is the strongest single subsystem in Sutra and would survive a handoff to a serious engineering team intact.
### 2. The assistant safety boundary is thoughtfully layered (preserve)
src/features/assistant/assistant-safety.js + action-system.js + assistant-permissions.js + note-patch-system.js + sutra-assistant-memory.js. The assistant never auto-executes — every action goes through previewPlan → user review → applyPlan with stateFingerprint freshness check (action-system.js:369-371), explicit confirmation tiers (requiresConfirmation for always/writes/destructive), idempotency journal keyed by plan:<previewId> (:296, :384-387), reverse-order rollback (:314-353), and partial_rollback reporting. wrapUntrusted/defangFence (assistant-safety.js:227) closes the classic "data exfiltration via fence-closing" hole by replacing < with ‹ inside any value that tries to forge or close the <<<SUTRA_UNTRUSTED_DATA label="...">>>>...<<<END_SUTRA_UNTRUSTED_DATA>>> wrapper. The memory classifier (sutra-assistant-memory.js:157-190) refuses to ever store blocked-class content (passwords, sk-/ghp_/xox tokens, CVV/CVC/routing/IBAN/SWIFT/SSN, medical diagnoses/prescriptions/meds, lat/long, 13–19-digit credit-card-shaped runs) and only stores sensitive-class content (home address, phone, DOB) with explicit user consent. Secret-redaction regexes (assistant-safety.js:8-14) cover OpenAI/Anthropic/Groq/xAI/Perplexity/Gemini key shapes plus Bearer, plus URL-embedded ?key=…/?access_token=… (error-reporter.js:63-68).
### 3. The persistence pipeline is paranoid in the right ways (preserve)
commitAppDataWithHealth (app.js:7195) runs every commit through a single FIFO queue; serializes appData once into an immutable JSON string; parses a detached snapshot so a mutation on live appData during the async write/readback window cannot alter what was stored; performs a writeIf conditional write inside a single readwrite transaction with predicate hashCanonicalWorkspaceRecord(current) === canonicalWorkspaceHash to detect cross-tab writes; advances canonicalWorkspaceHash only after the atomic commit; performs a separate readback verification with hashPersistenceString(storedText) !== summary.hash → PartialWriteError; records dataHealth with attempt/success/failure timestamps; clears failure state on success only if shouldClearPersistenceFailureOnSuccess(reason); notifies Drive/Cloud/Sync in independent try/catch blocks so a sync failure can never block local saving. The persistence state machine exposes the failure to the user via a "could not confirm your last save" data-safety banner. This is exactly the right design for a local-first product where data loss is the one unforgivable failure.
### 4. The DOM safety layer is one of the best-engineered in the codebase (preserve)
src/core/dom-safety.js (527 LOC). Tag allowlist excludes script-bearing tags by removing their subtree (not unwrapping), so executable payloads cannot survive. Attributes are default-deny with GLOBAL_ATTRS + per-tag allowlist + aria-* (+ opt-in data-*). URL attributes are re-validated against a scheme allowlist (javascript:/vbscript:/data:/blob:/file: blocked) and URL_NOISE strips control characters to defeat java\tscript: obfuscation. Inline style is parsed via a probe element, then property-by-property re-validated against SAFE_STYLE_PROPERTIES with url()/expression()/behavior/-moz-binding/@import/javascript:/vbscript:/data:/var() blocked. User id/class attributes are namespaced so user CSS/JS cannot target app selectors. Anchors opening new tabs get rel="noopener noreferrer". Sandboxed iframe rendering (renderUserHTMLToFrame:479-504) uses sandbox="" by default. The CI guardrail sutra-dom-integrity-check.mjs treats ad-hoc el.innerHTML = … as failures, and setTrustedHTML is the audited escape hatch (:420-424) — the only sanctioned raw-innerHTML channel.
### 5. The encrypted-backup envelope is correctly built (preserve)
encryptSutraPackageBytesWithKey (app.js:55145) uses AES-GCM-256 with 96-bit random IVs, 128-bit auth tag, additionalData = headerBytes (so header tampering fails decryption), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with random 16-byte salt. decryptSutraEncryptedEnvelopeBytes re-derives the key per envelope so KDF iterations can be advanced per-envelope without breaking old backups. The 12-category tamper matrix in tests/e2e/sutra-envelope-tamper.spec.mjs:82-130 verifies every malformed envelope is rejected before any plaintext is produced. The SutraDecryptError name is always thrown on decryption failure (constant message — never reveals the failure mode).
### 6. The release pipeline is reproducible and genuinely verified (preserve)
build:deploy is deny-by-default allowlist (build-deploy-artifact.mjs); .deploy/ is rebuilt from scratch every run (rmSync(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true })); pre-flight asserts every required source exists, post-copy asserts each landed in .deploy/; CI uploads the verified-deploy-${{ github.sha }} artifact, the browser-tests job downloads that exact artifact and serves it via SUTRA_SERVE_ROOT=.deploy, so e2e tests run against the exact bytes that ship to GitHub Pages; the deploy workflow does NOT rebuild in the deploy job (enforced by check-workflows.mjs); live-smoke waits for HTTP 200 then runs npm run check:live against the deployed URL. SHA-pinned actions, cancel-in-progress: true, cache: npm, job-scoped permissions. The cache-stamp lock (scripts/cache-stamp-lock.json — 162 entries with content hashes) prevents the "edited file, forgot to bump ?v=" cache-staleness bug.
### 7. The service worker is paranoid in the right ways (preserve)
sw.js uses cache.addAll(CRITICAL_ASSETS) which rejects on any failure (so a partially cached application never takes control); OPTIONAL_ASSETS use Promise.allSettled so cosmetic failures don't invalidate the shell; activate deletes all sutra-cache-* keys not equal to the current version; the fetch handler only intercepts same-origin GETs, never touches cross-origin (so AI providers, Drive, OAuth all bypass); navigations are network-first with cache fallback; versioned assets are cache-first with ignoreSearch: false; only res.type === 'basic' responses are cached (never opaque); the Share Target handler enforces SHARE_MAX_FILES=8, SHARE_MAX_FILE_SIZE=20MB, SHARE_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE=30MB, validates file types against an allowlist, sanitizes title/text/url lengths, requires https?:// for URLs, computes a SHA-256 fingerprint for dedup within 10 minutes, and 24-hour TTL cleanup. Records persist in dedicated sutra_share_target_db IDB — never cached, never forwarded.
### 8. custom-tabs.js demonstrates the right architecture pattern (preserve and replicate)
src/features/workspace/custom-tabs.js (2,510 LOC) opens with: "DOM is built exclusively with createElement/textContent (guardrail: zero unsafe innerHTML sinks in this file). No direct localStorage/sessionStorage access; all state rides the bridge." It uses document-level event delegation so overflow-menu clones keep working. It manages per-widget live timers with explicit cleanup on re-render and view change. This is the model the rest of src/features/workspace/*.js should follow — and the contrast with business-workspace.js:1960 (innerHTML = with escapeText per field) shows what the team is capable of when they take the time.
### 9. The 16-landmine AGENTS.md "Known architectural landmines" section (preserve as a document, do not interpret as completeness)
AGENTS.md:613-631 is a remarkable artifact — a maintainer-authored list of the 16 specific ways a naive change to Sutra can break user data, leak content across views, or break the service worker. Landmine #13 ("Canvas pages visually leak note content through the V2 editor host") and #14 ("Slides has its own author-level display rule") are exactly the kind of context a future contributor needs. This document is the single best argument for keeping app.js small enough to reason about — but it's also evidence of how many implicit invariants the codebase has accumulated.
## What Is MID
### 1. feature-registry.js is well-designed but only governs two features
src/features/feature-registry.js (134 LOC) is a clean lazy-loader with dependency resolution, init/teardown lifecycle, and per-feature metrics. But feature-manifest.js declares only **two** features (business, assistant). Everything else (Today, Homework, Notes, Timeline, Courses, AllDue, Life, College, APStudy, Review, CramHub, Assistant View, Settings) is statically loaded by <script> tags in Sutra.html. The registry pattern exists but isn't applied to the bulk of the codebase. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — extend the manifest to govern more features incrementally.
### 2. The "contract test" pattern is ratchet theatre masquerading as behavior testing
~8 unit tests (tests/unit/onboarding-contract.test.mjs, unencrypted-sutra-export.test.mjs, sync-account-isolation.test.mjs, sync-boundary-audit-contract.test.mjs, duress-lock-screen-entry.test.mjs, ics-import-size-contract.test.mjs, startup-health-contract.test.mjs, guardrail-global-contract.test.mjs) use tests/helpers/extract-function.mjs (a hand-rolled brace-matching parser) to pull a function body out of the 85k-line app.js and then assert.match(body, /…/). They prove the string is in the source, not that the runtime behaves that way. A future refactor that extracts the body to a separate module, renames variables, or wraps the call in a condition will break these tests even if behavior is preserved; conversely, dead code containing the right string passes. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — convert these to behavior tests against extracted pure functions.
### 3. The "property-fuzz" test is a deterministic LCG with 250–500 iterations
tests/unit/property-fuzz.test.mjs:10-16 defines random() as Math.imul(state, 1664525) + 1013904223 (an LCG). It only fuzzes homework.normalizeWorkspace, migrations.migrateWorkspace, and actions.validate — none of sync-merge, sync-engine, sync-crypto, sync-projection, the .sutra envelope parser, or assistant-safety.auditRequest. No shrinking, no minimum-failure examples. The "typed actions reject a deterministic corpus of malicious URLs" at :73-95 is a hardcoded list, not property-based. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — adopt fast-check or similar.
### 4. The 26 themes system is technically a feature but operationally a sprawl
26 distinct [data-theme="..."] selectors in styles/base/styles.css (lines 171–527+), plus signature presets (styles/themes/signature-presets.css), plus brand themes (theme-cohesion.css), plus 7 legacy CSS files. Per the June 2026 internal audit (docs/audits/UI_UX_POLISH_AUDIT_2026-06.md:22): "--space-1..7 scale exists but is used ~14 times against ~2,000 hardcoded px values; zero font-size tokens; zero z-index tokens (one value is 2147483000)." The audit identified this; the audit is two months old; the issue persists. **Severity: Medium. Eventual redesign** — derive semantic tokens per theme, audit hardcoded values.
### 5. Modal management is centralized but only for ~25 hand-registered selectors
SutraModalManager (app.js:38798-39119) auto-injects role="dialog", aria-modal="true", tabindex="-1", manages focus stack, traps Tab + Escape, restores focus on close. The selector list (contracts.css:21-50 and app.js:38799-38829) must be hand-synced — drift is silent. Open detection is class-name-driven (aria-hidden="false" OR .active OR .fs-visible OR .is-visible). Anything using .show, [open], hidden=false, or just toggling inline display is invisible to the manager. New modals that don't use the right signal class bypass focus management. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — converge on one "open" signal, or automate selector discovery.
### 6. The setTrustedHTML channel relies on developer discipline, not an enforced invariant
setTrustedHTML (dom-safety.js:420-424) IS raw el.innerHTML. It's the audited escape hatch for trusted dev markup. The pattern is "dev-controlled markup + esc()-escaped dynamic values." There's no automated check that output of buildPreviewHtml, renderMarkdown, or the 391 innerHTML writes in app.js is sanitized before reaching the DOM sink. A missed esc() in any future action preview, receipt, or markdown extension would let model-controlled JSON inject script. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — add a static-analysis check that every setTrustedHTML/innerHTML sink either routes through sanitizeUserHTML or carries a sutra-allow-html annotation that requires escaping invariants.
### 7. notifications.js mixes SutraSafeStorage and direct innerHTML
2 localStorage. calls and 6 SutraSafeStorage calls in 1,785 lines. Empty-state markup uses inline onclick="if(typeof setActiveView==='function') setActiveView('today')" (notifications.js:557) — bypassing the customization safe-mode and the safe-storage bridge. Per-row HTML is built via template strings with _esc() per field (lines 575-604) — correct, but the same brittle pattern as business-workspace.js:1960. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — convert to createElement/textContent per the custom-tabs.js pattern.
### 8. The 142 console.warn(...) swallow points
Across app.js, view renderers wrap per-view render in try { ... } catch (e) { console.warn('renderX failed on view change', e); } (app.js:32676, 32690, 32694, 32697, 32700 for 7 consecutive views). This is fail-soft — the user keeps working — but fail-silent. No error surface, no retry affordance, no telemetry. The June 2026 audit recommended a real error boundary; nothing happened. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — wrap views in a SutraViewErrorBoundary that surfaces a retry affordance.
### 9. The core-runtime-integrity.mjs size floor is the wrong shape of guard
scripts/lib/core-runtime-integrity.mjs:5-6 asserts src/core/app.js is **at least 4.5 MB and 80,000 lines**. This is a size floor, not a quality gate — a 5 MB monolith with 353 unsafe sinks passes the floor. The REQUIRED_FRAGMENTS list (:8-31) is string-include checks (text.includes('window.SutraSync = {')), so a comment containing that string would satisfy the check. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — invert the direction: assert a ceiling not a floor, then shrink the ceiling as app.js is decomposed.
### 10. Two parallel navigation taxonomies for the same destinations
The top-row More menu groups destinations as Daily loop / Learning / Workspace / My dashboards / Tools (Sutra.html:473-502). The mobile More sheet re-sorts to ['today', 'homework', 'notes', 'timeline', 'apstudy', 'settings'] (mobile-nav.js:76) so "Homework never gets pushed behind business/advanced views on a phone." Two parallel taxonomies for the same destinations is a real source of user confusion. **Severity: Medium. Incremental cleanup** — pick one canonical order and apply it everywhere.
## What Is BAD
### 1. The 85,392-line src/core/app.js monolith (Critical)
src/core/app.js is one file with 227 top-level functions, 31 window.Sutra* exports, 391 innerHTML writes, 774 addEventListener calls, 129 setTimeout/setInterval calls, 142 console.warn swallow points, 14 localStorage.setItem direct writes, 54 JSON.parse calls, 90 JSON.stringify calls. The AGENTS.md :615 admits "src/core/app.js is large and closure-coupled. Some controllers remain there because they need private helpers. Extract only after tracing dependencies and adding tests." The 4.5 MB / 80k-line **size floor** in core-runtime-integrity.mjs:5-6 **actively prevents extraction** — shrinking the file below the floor fails CI. Satellite UI files like student-loop-actions.js:3-7 open with "kept outside core/app.js so safe HTML event-handler cleanup does not make the global runtime even larger" — a convention that concedes the file is too big for new UI glue. **Localized vs systemic:** Systemic. Every other BAD finding is downstream of this one. **Severity: Critical.** Architectural — requires a real extraction plan with regression-tested seams, not the current "core:worktree" workflow that adds work but doesn't shrink the monolith.
### 2. script-src 'unsafe-inline' in CSP amplifies every DOM-sink bug (High)
scripts/lib/csp-policy.mjs:21 and Sutra.html:6. Documented as "temporarily required by legacy inline handlers" with a ratchet (scripts/sutra-csp-check.mjs + per-file INLINE_CODE_BUDGETS, Sutra.html ceiling: 7 inline scripts). Today, however, 'unsafe-inline' remains. Any XSS — from a missed esc() in buildPreviewHtml, renderMarkdown, or any of the 391 innerHTML sites in app.js, or from a third-party script on cdnjs/unpkg/accounts.google.com — runs with full origin privileges. The 264 inline onclick= handlers in Sutra.html cannot be removed safely without an event-delegation refactor (which custom-tabs.js already proves is the right pattern). **Localized vs systemic:** Systemic. **Severity: High.**
### 3. Cross-tab workspace writes race on browsers without Web Locks (High)
src/persistence/workspace-coordinator.js:64-72. When navigator.locks is unavailable (Safari < 16.4, older mobile WebViews — still meaningful iOS share), runExclusive falls back to a per-tab Promise queue. Two tabs can both read the same baseline, both writeIf predicates accept, and the second put overrides the first with no conflict signal — only workspaceMeta.lastWriterTabId hints at the loss. **Localized vs systemic:** Localized to the fallback path but the consequence (silent data loss) is severe. **Severity: High.**
### 4. verifyDatabasesGone lies on Firefox/Safari (High)
src/persistence/revocation-wipe.js:68-75. verifyDatabasesGone returns true early if factory.databases is not a function (if (!factory || typeof factory.databases !== 'function') return true;). Firefox and Safari do not implement navigator.storage.databases(). The wipe then writes the complete guard even though a deleteDatabase call may have silently failed. A revoke-and-wipe — advertised as a security guarantee — may leave encrypted sync state, the wrapped vault key blob, and sutra_credentials_db (assistant API keys, refresh token) on the device. The user sees "complete" in the guard. The DATABASES array at revocation-wipe.js:6-14 is also hardcoded and does not include sutra_workspace_db (the canonical workspace DB name is noteflow_atelier_db) — if a future Sutra version adds a new IDB, revoked devices will retain that data. **Localized vs systemic:** Localized. **Severity: High.**
### 5. The credential vault's per-profile key has no passphrase prompt for read (High)
src/core/credential-vault.js:181-192, 341-361. The per-profile AES-GCM-256 key is generated once via crypto.subtle.generateKey, stored non-extractable in meta.encryptionKey, and used to encrypt every credential. getValue calls ensureKey() and decrypts with no user prompt. The WebCrypto extractable: false flag prevents export of the key but **does not prevent use** — any script running in the Sutra origin (XSS, compromised third-party dependency) can call crypto.subtle.decrypt through the key and silently exfiltrate every stored assistant API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, etc.) and the Sutra Cloud refresh token. **Localized vs systemic:** Architectural threat-model boundary. **Severity: High.** Document the threat model explicitly OR add a passphrase/PIA gate in front of getValue.
### 6. Background not inert when modals open (High — WCAG 2.4.3 / 2.1.2)
src/core/app.js:38918-38921 (syncScrollLock toggles only body.sutra-modal-lock + body.modal-open). inert is only applied to the sidebar in contextual-shell.js:41,64,65 and app.js:19905,19908. When any of the ~25 modal-selector surfaces opens, the rest of the page stays focusable. Screen-reader virtual-buffer navigation and reading mode will visit background content while the user believes they are in a modal dialog. body.modal-open { overflow: hidden !important; } (styles.css:2616) only prevents mouse scrolling, not focus or AT navigation. The SutraModalManager does manage Tab and Escape inside the modal — but a screen-reader user browsing by virtual cursor can still read the underlying Today view through an open modal. **Localized vs systemic:** Systemic across all 25+ modal surfaces. **Severity: High.**
### 7. Two parallel token systems, neither enforced (High)
styles/base/tokens.css (90 lines, defines --sutra-*) vs styles/base/styles.css:7-105 (defines --space-*, --text-*, --radius, --transition-*) plus 13 more :root blocks inside styles.css (at lines 8830, 9064, 9115, 14020, 14044, 14298, 21310, 21850, 21903, 22642, 27096, 31194, 32000). var(--sutra-*) appears in meaningful numbers only in styles/views/contextual-shell.css (120 uses); styles/base/styles.css (35,315 lines) uses it **once**. The actual theming happens via --bg-primary/--accent/--text-primary (defined 292 times in styles.css across 26 themes). Hardcoded cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) (the value of --transition-fast) is repeated literally dozens of times. z-index literals outnumber var(--z-*) by ~250:8 across the codebase; styles/themes/sutra-pro.css alone has 21 raw z-index values including 99998, 2147483000, 99990. font-family: is declared 56 times in styles.css with at least 5 different stacks. **Localized vs systemic:** Systemic. **Severity: High.** Eventual redesign.
### 8. styles/legacy/ — 3,137 lines of acknowledged debt shipped to production (Medium-High)
All six files in styles/legacy/ carry the same header (e.g. app-shell-base.css:1-3): "Extracted from Sutra.html inline <style data-sutra-inline-style-legacy=...>. Loaded by a <link> at the SAME cascade position in Sutra.html, so the visual result is identical. Legacy block kept whole; split incrementally." Loaded in production: Sutra.html:132, 7612, 7761, 7763, 7765, 7782. The "split incrementally" comment is dated 20260616-cssextract1. The split never happened. Each legacy file has its own breakpoint scale (app-shell-base.css uses 1500/1200/980/860/640; responsive-hardening.css uses 1920/1366/1180/1024/900/768/640/720). refinement.css:13-45 forces sidebar transform: translateX(-108%) !important on <=1024px, which means the "real" sidebar CSS in styles.css cannot be edited safely without knowing the legacy override is layered on top. **Localized vs systemic:** Systemic debt. **Severity: Medium-High** (escalates to High if the codebase keeps growing without the split).
### 9. The legacy-workspace-migration promise that never resolves (Medium)
src/boot/legacy-workspace-migration.js:256-297, 299-323. The migration promise is set up in an IIFE at module load. If it rejects (IDB open failure, JSON parse failure on legacy localStorage, a corrupted CONFIRMED_ROOT_KEY marker), the .catch(error => console.warn(...)) at line 295 logs but **does not resolve or replace** the promise. Every subsequent db.read/db.write/db.writeIf calls waitForMigration() which awaits the rejected promise — every canonical workspace operation rejects with the original error forever. After a one-time migration failure, the workspace becomes unloadable in this browser profile; the user cannot recover without manual IDB inspection. The only signal is a console.warn at boot. **Localized vs systemic:** Localized. **Severity: Medium.**
### 10. chaos-persistence.spec.mjs provides no real chaos coverage (Medium)
tests/e2e/chaos-persistence.spec.mjs:17-39, 41-55, 115-160, 219-237, 241-262. Every test boils down to await page.waitForTimeout(1500/2000) then expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.body.children.length > 0)).toBeTruthy(). The "corruption" test seeds localStorage.setItem('noteflow_atelier_db', '{{CORRUPT') and asserts only that some UI rendered after a 2-second wait. The "DOM integrity" test asserts afterCount < beforeCount 3 after switching views 10 times — a "no runaway leak" check, not a correctness check. None of these tests assert data integrity, error recovery semantics, or specific UI states — they would pass against an app that displays a blank page. The chaos-persistence name suggests coverage that doesn't exist. *Localized vs systemic:** Localized. **Severity: Medium.**
### 11. The guardrail pattern ratchets in 427 unsafe DOM sinks (Medium)
scripts/lib/guardrail-scan.mjs is line/regex-based. scripts/guardrail-baseline.json:17 ratchets in **353** innerHTML= calls and **15** direct localStorage.setItem calls in src/core/app.js alone, plus 427 unsafe sinks total across the runtime. The "guardrail" only fails CI if the count grows — it does not require migration to SutraDOMSafety or SutraSafeStorage. The inline escape hatch (// sutra-allow-html: <reason>, guardrail-scan.mjs:15-19) silences a finding entirely with no review gate. A refactor that swaps one innerHTML = for outerHTML = (still a sink) keeps the count flat and passes. This is ratchet theatre, not a security gate. **Localized vs systemic:** Systemic. **Severity: Medium.**
### 12. HomePage.html is a separate 3,892-line design system (Medium)
HomePage.html (lines 102–2035 and 2037–2523) carries its own ~2,000 lines of inline <style> with its own token system (--bg: #04060b, --accent: #5078f2, --font-sans, --radius-sm/md/lg), its own breakpoints, and zero sharing with the app. Maintaining two design systems doubles every visual decision. The marketing surface and the product surface look related but are mechanically unrelated. **Localized vs systemic:** Localized. **Severity: Medium.**
## Architecture Assessment
Sutra's architecture is **a static SPA with eight well-factored subsystems and one massive runtime monolith glued on top**:
1. **Entry layer** (Sutra.html 8,915 lines + 105 <script> tags + 44 <link> stylesheets) — declarative, no build, classic scripts.
2. **Safety layer** (src/core/{error-reporter,dom-safety,feature-guard,recovery-mode,workspace-lock,safe-storage,startup-health,issue-prompt,credential-vault,credential-vault-bridge,migrations}.js) — zero-dependency IIFEs, load before everything else, never throw.
3. **Domain layer** (src/domain/ — homework-store, student-engine, workspace-entity-registry, planner, mastery, learning-engine, student-life, icalendar, import-engine, assistant-permissions, notes-knowledge-core) — pure data normalizers and engines, no DOM, no storage.
4. **Persistence layer** (src/persistence/ — workspace-db, workspace-coordinator, revocation-wipe, storage-hygiene + src/boot/legacy-workspace-migration.js) — IndexedDB + Web Locks + BroadcastChannel; canonical workspace DB is noteflow_atelier_db (legacy name preserved).
5. **Sync layer** (src/sync/sync-{protocol,crypto,projection,diff,merge,store,transport,engine}.js + supabase/sync-schema.sql) — E2E-encrypted multi-device sync over Supabase RPC; pure modules, headless-tested.
6. **Assistant layer** (src/features/assistant/ — assistant-core, assistant-safety, action-system, note-patch-system, sutra-assistant-memory, sutra-capability-registry, sutra-product-knowledge, sutra-local-help, model-capabilities, intelligence-diagnostics, flow-intelligence, flow-assistant [8,580 LOC]) — layered with explicit safety boundary.
7. **Feature layer** (src/features/{workspace,study,academic,customization,notes}/) — satellite UI modules, mostly IIFE + window.Sutra* global.
8. **Runtime monolith** (src/core/app.js — 85,392 LOC) — owns routing, hydration, persistence commit, theming, modal manager, toast, tutorial, chatbot FAB, onboarding, encrypted backup, Drive sync, Cloud sync bridge, ~12 per-view renderers, hundreds of normalizers, the markdown renderer, and 31 window.Sutra* exports.
Layers 1–7 have clean boundaries and dependency direction (safety → domain → persistence → sync; assistant depends on domain + safety; features depend on persistence + domain). Layer 8 is the glue that violates the boundaries — it touches storage directly (localStorage.setItem 14 times), manipulates the DOM (innerHTML 391 times), manages theming, and re-implements renderers that satellite files also implement (renderBusinessWorkspace in app.js:22400 and business-workspace.js:render() — app.js falls back to its own implementation if window.NoteFlowBusiness is unavailable, so two parallel render paths exist for the same view).
What has scaled well: sync, persistence, assistant safety, encrypted backup, the service worker. These would survive a handoff to a serious engineering team intact.
What is starting to strain: app.js size (and the size floor that prevents reduction); the parallel style systems; the modal selector hand-sync; the inline-handler coupling to customization safe-mode; the 26-theme sprawl; the duplicated navigation taxonomies; the source-text-regex test pattern; the 427-sink guardrail baseline.
## Code Quality Assessment
**Maintainability:** Mixed. Domain/persistence/sync modules are tight (typically 100–600 LOC, single responsibility, well-commented). The runtime monolith is the maintainability bottleneck — 227 functions, 391 innerHTML sinks, 31 window.Sutra* exports, no module boundary, no test coverage measurement.
**Complexity:** sync-engine.performCycle (~290 LOC, app.js:7195 → performCommitAppDataWithHealth is ~100 LOC with FIFO queue + conditional write + readback verification + health state + Drive/Cloud/Sync notification in independent try/catches + lifecycle journal + persistence failure recording) and sync-merge.merge (~285 LOC, sync-merge.js:749) are large but necessary. flow-assistant.js at 8,580 LOC is large but well-organized (named sections, clear header). app.js is unreasonably large.
**Duplication:**
- renderBusinessWorkspace exists in both app.js:22400 and business-workspace.js — fallback pattern.
- The modal selector list is duplicated in contracts.css:21-50 and app.js:38799-38829 — must be hand-synced.
- Six variants of .empty-state markup with class names .empty-state, .chat-empty-state, .cw-empty-state, .th2-empty-state, .timeline-empty-state, .drawer-empty.
- escapeText/escapeHtml defined independently in app.js (twice — at lines 40558 and 71880), business-workspace.js:299, slides.js:46-47 (where escapeText is misnamed — it just trims whitespace, then escapeHtml calls it before escaping — confusing but not buggy).
- Two parallel token systems (--sutra-* vs --space-*/--text-*/--radius).
**Abstraction quality:** Strong in the assistant action system (ACTION_CATALOG data-driven, separate sutra-capability-registry.js for per-action metadata). Strong in sync (protocol/engine/merge/diff/projection/transport/store separated cleanly). Weak in UI — no Button/Card/Dialog/Tooltip/Tabs/FormField components. data-sutra-component is set on only six elements; treated as a tagging marker, not consumed by any registry.
**Naming:** Generally good. Legacy "NoteFlow"/"Atelier"/"flowAtelier"/"flow-assistant" names survive (the file is flow-assistant.js but the global is sutraAssistant); legacy "noteflow_atelier_db" IndexedDB name is preserved for migration safety (correct decision). escapeText in slides.js is misnamed.
**Comments:** Extensive and high-quality. The "why" is documented in critical paths (workspace-coordinator.js comments on race semantics; sync-engine.js comments on the deliberate-pause-wins-over-auth-error invariant at line 580; dom-safety.js header documents the trust model). The AGENTS.md "Known architectural landmines" section is a remarkable artifact.
**Technical debt:** See the Technical Debt Map below.
## Reliability / Data Integrity Assessment
This is one of Sutra's strongest areas, with three real holes.
**Strong:**
- commitAppDataWithHealth (app.js:7195) is exemplary: FIFO queue, detached immutable snapshot, conditional write inside atomic tx, separate readback verification, PartialWriteError/WorkspaceConflictError/WorkspaceReadSafetyError named errors with user-facing explanations.
- sync-engine.runCycle's catch block (app.js:575-613 later in the file, or the equivalent in sync-engine.js) classifies errors into update-required/auth-expired/unauthorized/quota-exceeded/schema-mismatch/snapshot-required/revoked/encryption-error/conflict-storm and surfaces each to a specific UI state.
- sync-engine's conflict-store-failure path aborts before apply/push/baseline-advance (verified by unit test sync-engine.test.mjs:266-297).
- sync-store.commitCycleState is a single multi-store readwrite transaction — a crash can never leave a half-advanced sync state.
- Stale-cursor race is bounded at 3 retries then stale-cursor + scheduleRetry().
- Conflict-storm circuit breaker pauses after 8 novel conflicts in 60s.
- Tombstone retention is 90 days.
- Encrypted-backup envelope uses AES-GCM-256 with 96-bit random IVs and AAD-bound headers — every malformed envelope is rejected before plaintext is produced (12-category tamper matrix test).
- legacy-workspace-migration.js monkey-patches SutraWorkspaceDB.create to run migration once per profile (problem: see BAD #9).
**Real holes:**
1. Cross-tab writes race on browsers without Web Locks (BAD #3).
2. verifyDatabasesGone lies on Firefox/Safari (BAD #4).
3. legacy-workspace-migration.js migration promise that never resolves (BAD #9).
4. sync-store.clearAll for scoped accounts iterates each STORE separately — partial failure leaves account B's state inconsistent; no test covers this (severity Low-Medium).
5. safe-storage.js "important" classification keeps the value in memory only — if the tab closes before backup, the in-memory change is lost (severity Low-Medium).
6. sync-engine.maybeCompact swallows errors via /* compaction is opportunistic, never fatal */ — repeated compaction failures cause ops to accumulate past COMPACT_EVERY_OPS=500 until snapshot-required eventually trips (severity Low).
## Testing Assessment
Test quantity is high: 91 unit tests, 92 e2e specs, 1 bench spec. Test quality is genuinely strong in the sync/persistence/assistant-safety/DOM-safety paths and genuinely weak in coverage breadth and source-text-regex patterns.
**Real behavior tests:**
- sync-crypto.test.mjs (224 LOC): AES-GCM AAD binding relabel detection, IV uniqueness across 200 envelopes.
- sync-merge.test.mjs (571 LOC): three-device convergence, server-reordered same-key ops still resolve to higher Lamport winner, pulled-back own-echo handling.
- sync-engine.test.mjs (806 LOC): offline queue/retry, idempotency, conflict-storm breaker, delete-edit, stale-cursor race, busy save defer, future schema pause, tampered envelope abort, revoked pause, deliberate pause precedence, jitter, locked engine, snapshot bootstrap.
- assistant-action-system.test.mjs: three-action plan with third failing asserts rollback in reverse order ['commit:a','commit:b','commit:c','rollback:b','rollback:a'].
- sutra-envelope-tamper.spec.mjs:82-130: 12-category single-field tamper matrix.
- dom-safety.spec.mjs:15-38: 21 hostile payloads through SutraDOMSafety.sanitizeUserHTML.
- locked-note-privacy.spec.mjs:120-132: locked note plaintext never reaches editor/search/review generator/backlinks/canvas linked cards/slides.
- cloud-sync.spec.mjs (1,653 LOC): two-real-browser-context sync with the **same in-memory transport server** the unit tests exercise — mock is realistic, not a separate stub.
**Weak tests:**
- 8 source-text-regex "contract" tests (MID #2).
- property-fuzz.test.mjs deterministic LCG (MID #3).
- chaos-persistence.spec.mjs asserts only "page rendered" (BAD #10).
**Coverage gaps:**
- No coverage measurement (no --coverage, no c8, no nyc).
- No unit-level encrypted-backup crypto tests — only e2e.
- No tests for the 391 innerHTML sinks in app.js.
- No tests for the Background Sync API (sw.js:296-306).
- No tests for Share Target negative paths (oversized, unsupported type, unsafe URL).
- No tests for offline outbox replay in sync-engine.js.
- assistant-permissions.test.mjs is only 45 lines / 4 tests — no mixed-mode transitions, persisted policy drift, destructive-action approval rejection.
Test quantity vs quality: **9/10 quantity, 6/10 quality** (would be 7-8 if the source-text-regex tests were converted to behavior tests).
## Performance Assessment
No virtual DOM, no Suspense, no skeleton states, no production telemetry. SutraSafeStorage is read synchronously so most views pop in.
**Likely current bottlenecks:**
- SutraModalManager MutationObserver observes document.documentElement subtree and runs syncAll() (a document.querySelectorAll(modalSelector) across 25 selectors) on every qualifying mutation. rAF coalesced but still scans the whole document on any mutation that touches a modal root.
- adjustChatbotPosition() (app.js:19842-19888) reads offsetParent, getComputedStyle().display, getBoundingClientRect() multiple times then writes style.left/right/bottom — invoked on every resize. Same pattern in positionSpacesDropdown(), positionTutorialReposition, updateScrollButtons (called from scroll/resize/mutation/Resize/MutationObserver — four sources). None batch reads/writes via rAF.
- 391 innerHTML writes mean many views do full template renders. business-workspace.js:2176 does root.innerHTML = ... with template strings.
- 8 separate scroll listeners and 22 resize listeners in app.js.
- The mobile-nav rebuilds the entire <nav> on every noteflow:view-changed event (mobile-nav.js:419 navEl.replaceChildren()) — fine for ~5 items.
- 26 themes × full re-render of [data-theme=] selectors — styles.css is 35k lines parsed once.
**Likely future bottlenecks:**
- The --space-* vs --sutra-* token duplication will compound as more themes are added.
- The 353 innerHTML sinks in app.js will compound as new features land.
- The bench (tests/bench/heavy-workspace.spec.mjs) has no baseline diffing — perf regressions are silent.
## Security & Privacy Assessment
**Strong:**
- E2E sync encryption: server never sees plaintext.
- All sync RPCs are security definer with set search_path = pg_catalog, public.
- sync_authorize_device binds JWT session_id to device row; unique index prevents one session driving two devices.
- sync_get_device_status deliberately does NOT call sync_authorize_device — returns only bounded status requiring the exact pre-revocation tuple; client validates validateVerifiedWipeInstruction against the expected project URL and identity before any local wipe.
- REST transport strips userId/ownerId from body before RPC.
- Storage RLS uses anchored regex ^<uid>/[0-9a-f]{64}$ plus sync_session_active().
- sync_put_vault_key checks keyId matches existing wrapped key — prevents replacement with a different key.
- DOM safety layer is one of the best-engineered in the codebase.
- Action system: schema validation, cycle detection, depth cap, payload size cap, containsMaliciousMarkup() regex, confirmation tiers, transactional commit/rollback, idempotency journal, target-snapshot freshness.
- Assistant memory classifier refuses to ever store blocked-class content.
- Secret-redaction regexes cover common provider key shapes plus URL-embedded keys.
- error-reporter.js deduped (4s window), secret-scrubbed (Gemini URL keys included), in-memory ring buffer (250 entries).
- safe-storage.js deliberately has no key-storage, vault, or export involvement.
**Concerns:**
- BAD #5: credential vault per-profile key decryptable by any same-origin script with no passphrase prompt.
- BAD #2: script-src 'unsafe-inline' amplifies any DOM-sink bug.
- BAD #4 + #6 (revocation wipe lying on Firefox/Safari): the advertised security guarantee is not delivered on those browsers.
- Workspace lock is a UX gate, not encryption-at-rest (acknowledged in code, but the UI affordance is stronger than the protection; 4–8 digit PIN is offline-brute-forceable by anyone with the PBKDF2 verifier).
- PBKDF2 600k iterations is at the OWASP 2023 floor; consider 1M+ for sensitive credentials.
- flow-intelligence.js:588 falls through to unredacted text if SutraAssistantSafety.redactText is unavailable — fail-open behavior is the wrong default for a privacy boundary.
- flow-assistant.js:7698-7701 hasAnyProviderConfigured() falls back to raw sessionStorage.getItem('groq_api_key' | 'openai_api_key' | 'anthropic_api_key' | 'gemini_api_key' | 'openrouter_api_key') — bypasses the credential vault and the safe-storage bridge. Values are only checked for presence, but the abstraction is broken.
## UI Audit
**Strongest aspects:**
- Per-surface visual styling is genuinely well-crafted. The Today dashboard, Timeline Calendar, Business Workspace, College App Tracker, AP Study, and Notes Editor each have thoughtful typography, spacing, and visual hierarchy. Screenshots in assets/screenshots/ confirm.
- The signature themes (Blueprint, Paper, Arcade in styles/themes/signature-presets.css) are authored visual systems, not accent-color swaps.
- The mobile-nav rebuilds the entire nav on every view change — predictable and clean. Pull-to-refresh, swipe between views, haptic feedback (with prefers-reduced-motion respect).
- The icon hydration system (src/components/icons/ — 553 registered icons) is the one reusable UI primitive that works: scans for <i class="fa-*"> and replaces with inline SVGs using currentColor so they follow themes.
- The contextual-shell pattern (contextual-shell.js) cleanly toggles inert on the sidebar when only Notes needs it — the one piece of IA reuse that works cleanly.
- Skip link, sr-only, primary nav with aria-label, real role="dialog" on the notifications panel with aria-expanded/aria-haspopup on the bell button, role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" on the toast, real role="dialog" modal management with focus stack and Tab/Escape trap.
- Carousel images on the landing page have descriptive alt; decorative copies correctly use aria-hidden="true" + alt="".
**Weakest aspects:**
- 264 inline onclick= handlers in Sutra.html (17 more in HomePage.html) — invisible to customization safe-mode, bypass safe-storage bridge, cannot be removed without event-delegation refactor.
- No reusable component layer — every view re-implements its own button (neumo-btn, cc-btn, hw-btn, ctab-action, today-hero-menu-item, view-tab, toolbar-btn, chatbot-icon-btn, nf-select-trigger, sutra-mobile-more-action).
- Empty states designed but not componentized — 6 variants of the same idea.
- Loading states essentially missing — aria-busy="true" is set in only two places. No skeleton, no per-view loading indicator.
- Error states collapse to showToast(message) — no error boundary, no retry affordance.
- Two parallel More menus (top-row More + mobile More sheet) with different groupings for the same destinations.
- forced-colors: active support in only 5 files; primary nav buttons lose their visual when forced colors are active.
- prefers-reduced-motion redundantly declared in contracts.css:99, mobile.css:768, 2437 — three places that should be one.
- HomePage.html carries its own ~2,000 lines of inline <style> with its own token system (BAD #12).
## UX Audit
Sutra's product surface feels **cohesive at the language level and fragmented at the interaction level**.
**Mental model:** "One private workspace, every thread" — clear and consistent. Local-first, no account, no telemetry. The product copy in README.md, HomePage.html, and in-product surfaces (Help & Docs, onboarding) reinforces this. The student-focused voice is calm and intentional.
**Information architecture:** Broad and shallow — 14 primary views plus Settings and Assistant destinations, plus user-composed custom tabs. Tab labels are inconsistent in naming style (Noun: "Home", "Homework", "Timeline", "College", "Life", "Business", "Courses", "Assistant", "Settings"; Verb: "Create" — Notes; Functional: "All Due" — icon-only; Hidden-retained-for-compat: "Review" and "Cram Hub" — buttons kept in markup but display:none "for backward-compat click handlers" (Sutra.html:454-455)). The duplicated navigation taxonomies (top-row More groups as Daily loop/Learning/Workspace/My dashboards/Tools; mobile More sheet re-sorts to today/homework/notes/timeline/apstudy/settings) is a real source of confusion.
**Feature discoverability:** Decent for the primary surfaces; weak for advanced features (Smart Import, Recovery Mode, Custom Tabs, Focus Session, Workspace Time Machine, Assignment Studio, Daily Lock-In Quote, Plugin SDK). The 47 docs in docs/features/ cover each feature in isolation; there is no "Start Here" surface that ties them together.
**Workflow friction:** Common actions are mostly 1-3 taps. Adding a task, opening a note, marking homework done, opening the assistant — all single-action. The friction emerges in recoverability: there is no undo for view renders (a try/catch that warns and continues is fail-silent, not fail-recoverable), no error boundary, no per-view error UI. The first-time experience is the onboarding overlay (app.js:26840+) which is well-built but asks the user to choose a Sutra Mode (Calm/Study/Everything) before they've seen the product.
**Cross-feature consistency:** Mixed. Today, Timeline, Homework, Notes feel like one product. Life, Business, College App, AP Study feel like four separate products glued into one shell — each has its own card style, its own button style, its own empty-state markup, its own render function (in app.js, except Business which delegates to business-workspace.js). The today-dashboard.js widget composition system (WIDGETS array, PRESETS Calm/Study/Everything) is the right pattern but only applies to Today.
**Implementation leakage:** The 4–8 digit PIN workspace lock is a UX gate marketed as "private workspace" — users with high threat models may over-trust it. The "Sutra Mode" picker at onboarding feels like an engineer's feature-flag surface exposed to users. The hidden #tabReview and #tabCramHub "for backward-compat click handlers" is dead UI in production markup — a UX debt visible to anyone reading the source.
**Recoverability:** Strong for persistence (data-safety banner, recovery mode, emergency export). Weak for view render errors (fail-silent console.warn).
**Destructive actions:** Action system requires explicit confirmation for destructive risk tier; confirmHighRiskAction opens a confirmVariant:'danger' dialog. The 4–8 digit workspace lock PIN is offline-brute-forceable. The .sutra export carries plaintext unless the user explicitly chooses encryption.
**Mobile workflows:** Mobile-nav is well-built (MAX_ITEMS=5, swipe, pull-to-refresh, haptic, focus-trapped More sheet, browser-Back integration). The mobile.css only contains view-specific rules for 4 of 14 views — the other 10 are covered only by generic patterns.
**First-time experience:** Onboarding overlay + Help & Docs + TUTORIAL.md + info.md + 47 feature docs + docs/README.md + AGENTS.md for contributors. The onboarding is well-designed; the documentation sprawl is not. There is no in-product "What's New" surface except SutraReleaseNotes (app.js:77187) hidden behind an undocumented interaction.
**Advanced-user experience:** Power features exist (Command Palette with fuzzy ranking + recent-commands ordering, Global Search, Smart Import paste wizard, Workspace Time Machine, Recovery Mode, Safe Mode for customization, Plugin SDK with .atelier-plugin files) — but discoverability is weak. examples/plugins/study-helper.atelier-plugin is the only plugin example.
## Mobile / Responsive Audit
**Convincing on phones for the four views with dedicated mobile CSS (Homework, Life, Notes, Timeline).** The mobile-nav rebuilds the nav cleanly, haptic feedback works, pull-to-refresh works, swipe between views works, iOS input zoom is prevented by bumping input font-size to 16px on <=768px (mobile.css:66-84), prefers-reduced-motion respected.
**Less convincing for the other ten views.** mobile.css (2,558 lines, 59 @media blocks) uses inconsistent breakpoints: 768px (22 times), 640px (19 times), 1024px (3 times), plus 360/400/480/900/359 (1-2 each). No breakpoint scale is documented in tokens.css (which defines spacing/type/shape/motion/z but **no breakpoints**). mobile-nav.js:44 treats max-width: 640px as mobile; sidebar-page-actions-menu.js:15 uses > 768 for desktop; primary-nav-visibility.js:15 uses >= 1441. Three different thresholds for the same concept.
@media (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse) suppresses hover transforms (good). forced-colors: active only honored in 5 files (calendar, contextual shell, html-pages, workspace-lock, plus a partial prefers-contrast: more block in styles.css:29674-29687 that only polishes Review cards). Windows High Contrast users get partial support.
The fixed Save/Export/Import bar on College/Life/Business hides the last content row — responsive-hardening.css:51-59 and mobile.css:1738-1741 add clearance via !important cascade (the June 2026 audit identified this; status: still present).
## Consistency Audit
**Interaction patterns:** Modal open signals are 4 different conventions (aria-hidden="false", .active, .fs-visible, .is-visible); 7 close-button conventions; the SutraModalManager "open" detection at app.js:38850-38862 uses class-name-driven detection.
**Visual patterns:** Two parallel token systems (BAD #7). 936 !important declarations in styles.css, 579 in mobile.css, 109 in contextual-shell.css. 8+ parallel button families each re-inventing primary/ghost/danger — 3 different danger reds, 2 disabled opacities, near-zero loading state. 56 hardcoded font-family: declarations in styles.css with at least 5 different stacks.
**Architectural patterns:** escapeHtml defined twice in app.js (lines 40558, 71880); escapeText defined in business-workspace.js:299 (escapes) and slides.js:46 (only trims whitespace, then escapeHtml calls it before escaping — confusing but not buggy). Render functions duplicated across app.js and satellite files (renderBusinessWorkspace).
**Naming:** Legacy "NoteFlow"/"Atelier"/"flowAtelier"/"flow-assistant" survive. The global is sutraAssistant but the file is flow-assistant.js. escapeText in slides.js is misnamed.
**State handling:** Persistence state machine is consistent (commitAppDataWithHealth → recordPersistenceSuccess/recordPersistenceFailure → dataHealth). The 142 console.warn(...) swallow points are inconsistent in their failure handling — some rethrow, some return null, some /* non-critical */, some if (typeof window.SutraReportError === 'function') window.SutraReportError(error, ...). The pattern is right (SutraReportError); the application is uneven.
**Duplicated systems:** Two parallel More menus. Two parallel token systems. renderBusinessWorkspace in two files. Modal selector list in contracts.css and app.js. Six empty-state class name variants.
## Technical Debt Map
**Low:**
- The escapeText misnaming in slides.js:46.
- safe-storage.js "important" classification keeping values in memory only.
- sync-engine.maybeCompact swallowing errors.
**Moderate:**
- The contract-test pattern (8 source-text-regex tests).
- The property-fuzz.test.mjs deterministic LCG.
- The 26-theme sprawl with hardcoded values.

- chaos-persistence.spec.mjs "page rendered" assertions.

- flow-assistant.js:7698-7701 raw sessionStorage fallback.
- The feature-manifest.js declaring only 2 features.
**Significant:**
- The 353 innerHTML sinks ratcheted in app.js (guardrail baseline).
- The 427 unsafe DOM sinks ratcheted across the runtime.
- The styles/legacy/ 3,137 lines of acknowledged-but-unpaid debt.
- The 936 !important declarations in styles.css.
- The 26 themes in a 35k-line file.
- The verifyDatabasesGone lying on Firefox/Safari.
- The cross-tab race on browsers without Web Locks.
- The legacy-workspace-migration promise that never resolves.

- The script-src 'unsafe-inline' in CSP.

**Structural:**
- The 85,392-line src/core/app.js monolith — the root cause of most other debt.
- The AGENTS.md 16 landmines — the codebase's implicit invariants that any change can violate.
- The two parallel style systems (token spine + 35k-line omnibus + legacy dir + theme dir + view dir + feature dir).
- The product waves (Sutra Cloud, Sutra Intelligence, Student OS upgrade, Today Redesign, Custom Tabs) that each added their own vocabulary and the consolidation never happened.
## Highest-Leverage Improvements
**1. Begin a real, regression-tested app.js decomposition plan.**
Problem: 85,392-line monolith with a CI size floor that prevents reduction (BAD #1).
Recommended direction: Pick a seams approach — extract SutraEncryptedBackups, SutraDriveSync, SutraCloudSync bridges (already namespaced at app.js:61914, 61969, 63566) into separate files. Each extraction is gated by npm run check:runtime (the existing worktree pattern), preserves byte-for-byte recovery, and shrinks the size floor in core-runtime-integrity.mjs. Start with the encrypted-backup extraction because sutra-envelope-tamper.spec.mjs already locks the behavior.
Expected impact: Unblocks every other improvement; future feature work lands in testable 200–600 LOC modules instead of an 85k-line file.
Rough scope: **Architectural** (multi-quarter effort, but each step is independently shippable).
**2. Move CSP to a nonce-based policy and convert the 7 inline scripts in Sutra.html to nonced <script> tags.**
Problem: script-src 'unsafe-inline' amplifies every DOM-sink bug (BAD #2).
Recommended direction: Add a per-request nonce (or per-build static nonce if GitHub Pages forces static), convert inline handlers to addEventListener via document-level event delegation (the custom-tabs.js pattern), remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src.
Expected impact: Closes the largest blast-radius amplifier for any XSS bug found elsewhere.
Rough scope: **Medium** (touches every inline handler in Sutra.html).
**3. Add an automated invariant: every setTrustedHTML/innerHTML sink must either route through sanitizeUserHTML or carry a sutra-allow-html: annotation that requires escaping invariants to be statically verified.**
Problem: The setTrustedHTML channel relies on developer discipline (MID #6); the guardrail baseline ratchets in 353 sinks without requiring migration (MID #11).
Recommended direction: Extend scripts/lib/guardrail-scan.mjs to read the sutra-allow-html: annotation, and add a static AST-level check (Babel parser, or even a stricter regex) that every ${...} interpolation in an allowed innerHTML template literal is wrapped in escapeHtml/esc/escapeText/sanitizeUserHTML. Fail CI on any unescaped interpolation.
Expected impact: Closes the "missed esc()" class of XSS.
Rough scope: **Medium**.
**4. Convert the 8 source-text-regex contract tests to behavior tests against extracted pure functions.**
Problem: Tests give false confidence; refactors that improve real safety may be blocked by failing string-matching tests (MID #2).
Recommended direction: Extract the function bodies into pure modules, write behavior tests against the modules. The contract tests then become regression tests on the module's public surface, not its source text.
Expected impact: Tests actually verify behavior; refactors can proceed without breaking tests.
Rough scope: **Medium** (each contract test is a 1-day extraction).
**5. Make verifyDatabasesGone fail-closed on Firefox/Safari and document the manual recovery flow.**
Problem: BAD #4 — advertised security guarantee not delivered on browsers without navigator.storage.databases().
Recommended direction: When factory.databases is unavailable, write a cleanup-error guard instead of complete, and surface a recovery banner with manual IDB-clear instructions. Add a test for the unavailable-API path.
Expected impact: Restores the revoke-and-wipe security guarantee on all browsers.
Rough scope: **Small**.
**6. Apply inert to background content when modals open.**
Problem: BAD #6 — WCAG 2.4.3 / 2.1.2 failure across all 25+ modal surfaces.
Recommended direction: In SutraModalManager.syncScrollLock, in addition to body.modal-open, set inert on <main> (or the equivalent container) when any modal is open. Add a test that asserts the background is not focusable while a modal is open.
Expected impact: WCAG conformance; restores the modal focus-trap contract for screen-reader users.
Rough scope: **Small-Medium**.
**7. Unify the token spine.**
Problem: Two parallel token systems, neither enforced (BAD #7).
Recommended direction: Make --sutra-* the canonical spine. Either (a) deprecate the --space-*/--text-*/--radius/--transition-* aliases by redefining them as references to --sutra-*, or (b) admit --sutra-* is aspirational and delete it. Add a CI check (extend scripts/sutra-app-shell-check.mjs or write a new one) that fails on hardcoded cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), hardcoded font-family: (outside :root), and raw z-index: <number> outside the contract list.
Expected impact: Every new theme preset requires editing a small semantic-token surface instead of a 35k-line file.
Rough scope: **Large** (touches every CSS file).
**8. Delete or genuinely split styles/legacy/.**
Problem: 3,137 lines of acknowledged-but-unpaid debt (BAD #8).
Recommended direction: For each legacy file, audit which selectors are still in use (via coverage tooling or grep against Sutra.html and app.js), move the in-use rules to the appropriate styles/base/, styles/views/, styles/features/, or styles/responsive/ file, and delete the legacy file. Update Sutra.html to remove the <link>.
Expected impact: Removes the "is this in use?" ambiguity; new contributors can read the styles directory and understand it.
Rough scope: **Medium-Large**.
**9. Route hasAnyProviderConfigured() and all credential access through providerMeta and the credential vault.**
Problem: flow-assistant.js:7698-7701 bypasses the abstraction (MID #10); flow-intelligence.js:588 fails open on redaction.
Recommended direction: Have providerMeta.hasAnyKey() enumerate from the same registry the CSP connect-src is built from. Make redactActivityText fail-*closed* (return '[redacted: safety module unavailable]') instead of failing open.
Expected impact: Single source of truth for provider key names; closes the fail-open redaction hole.
Rough scope: **Small**.
**10. Adopt fast-check (or similar) for property-based testing of sync-merge, sync-engine, sync-crypto, the .sutra envelope parser, and assistant-safety.auditRequest.**
Problem: property-fuzz.test.mjs is a deterministic LCG (MID #3).
Recommended direction: Replace the hand-rolled LCG with fast-check. Add shrinking. Fuzz the encrypted-backup envelope parser — the most security-sensitive code path — with adversarial byte sequences.
Expected impact: Catches deeply nested objects, oversized arrays, malformed strings that pass surface validation but break deeper layers.
Rough scope: **Medium**.
**11. Convert the 264 inline onclick= handlers in Sutra.html to addEventListener via document-level event delegation.**
Problem: Inline handlers are invisible to customization safe-mode, bypass safe-storage bridge, and force 'unsafe-inline' in CSP (improvement #2 depends on this).
Recommended direction: Use the custom-tabs.js document-level delegation pattern. Replace onclick="setActiveView('today')" with data-sutra-action="set-active-view" data-view="today" and a single delegated listener.
Expected impact: Closes the inline-handler coupling; enables CSP nonce migration.
Rough scope: **Large** (264 sites).
**12. Add a coverage tool (c8 or nyc) to npm run test:unit and surface coverage in CI.**
Problem: No coverage signal (MID testing); 391 innerHTML sinks in app.js may have zero behavioral coverage.
Recommended direction: Add c8 to devDependencies, run node --test with c8 instrumentation, fail CI if coverage of src/sync/, src/persistence/, src/domain/, src/core/dom-safety.js, src/core/credential-vault.js, src/features/assistant/assistant-safety.js, src/features/assistant/action-system.js drops below 80%.
Expected impact: Refactors can no longer silently drop coverage; new code that ships without tests fails CI.
Rough scope: **Small**.
**13. Consolidate navigation taxonomies.**
Problem: Two parallel More menus with different groupings (MID #10).
Recommended direction: Pick one canonical order and one canonical grouping (Daily loop / Learning / Workspace / My dashboards / Tools). Apply it to both the top-row More menu and the mobile More sheet. Re-order mobileTabs() in mobile-nav.js:76 to match.
Expected impact: One mental model for navigation across devices.
Rough scope: **Small**.
## Things I Would NOT Change
**1. The "no build, classic scripts, static hosting" philosophy.** This is the product's identity. Sutra is the only "if you can open an HTML file, you can run it" workspace of this scope. Any move to Vite/webpack/SSR would abandon the local-first-by-design principle. The 105 <script> tags are not debt — they are the architecture.
**2. The legacy IndexedDB name noteflow_atelier_db.** Preserving it is the correct migration-safety decision. Renaming would orphan every existing user's data.
**3. The sync protocol design** — lamport-based opIds, deterministic three-way merge, conflict-storm breaker, AAD-bound envelopes, security-definer RPCs, anchored-regex RLS, vault-key CAS, advisory locks per user, verified-wipe instruction. This is genuinely the strongest subsystem in Sutra. Any "rewrite sync in language X" proposal should be rejected.
**4. The action system's transactional model** — previewPlan → user review → applyPlan with stateFingerprint freshness, idempotency journal, reverse-order rollback, partial_rollback reporting. This is the right shape for an in-page workspace agent. Any "let the assistant apply directly" shortcut should be rejected.
**5. The encrypted-backup envelope format** — AES-GCM-256 with 96-bit random IV, AAD-bound headers, per-envelope KDF iterations, SutraDecryptError constant message. The 12-category tamper matrix test is the right shape of test for this surface. Preserve the format; do not "optimize" it.
**6. The persistence pipeline's writeIf conditional + readback verification + immutable detached snapshot.** This is exactly the right design for a local-first product. Do not "simplify" by removing the readback.
**7. The DOM safety layer's allowlist approach + namespaced user ids/classes + sandboxed iframe rendering.** Preserve the trust model. Do not "modernize" by switching to DOMPurify unless the replacement matches every invariant.
**8. The AGENTS.md "Known architectural landmines" document.** This is the single best argument for keeping app.js small enough to reason about. Preserve as a living document; do not turn it into a per-task activity log.
**9. The custom-tabs.js "zero unsafe innerHTML sinks, document-level event delegation, no direct localStorage/sessionStorage access" pattern.** This is the model the rest of src/features/workspace/*.js should follow. Replicate it, do not refactor it.
**10. The service worker's cache.addAll(CRITICAL_ASSETS) reject-on-failure + same-origin-only + network-first navigation + versioned-asset cache-first + Share Target defensive validation.** This is genuinely well-engineered. Preserve the strictness.
**11. The feature-registry.js lazy-loader with dependency resolution + init/teardown lifecycle + per-feature metrics.** Extend it to govern more features; do not replace it with a bundler.
**12. The token-aware cache-stamp lock (scripts/cache-stamp-lock.json with content hashes).** This prevents the "edited file, forgot to bump ?v=" cache-staleness bug. Preserve.
**13. The 14 view tabs and their dedicated render functions.** The breadth of features (Notes, Homework, Timeline, Today, AP Study, College App, Life, Business, Courses, All Due, Assistant, Review, Cram Hub, Settings, Custom Tabs) is the product's value proposition. Do not "consolidate" by removing views; consolidate by sharing components and tokens.
## Final Verdict
**How healthy is the codebase?** Mixed. The sync/persistence/assistant-safety/DOM-safety/service-worker/test pipeline is healthy and would survive a serious-engineering-team handoff intact. The 85k-line app.js monolith, the 35k-line styles.css, the two parallel token systems, and the ratchet-as-guardrail pattern are unhealthy and will compound as the codebase grows.
**Is the architecture still appropriate for Sutra's current size?** Layered architecture (safety → domain → persistence → sync; assistant depends on domain + safety; features depend on persistence + domain) is appropriate and well-factored. The monolithic runtime is not. The feature-registry.js pattern exists but governs only 2 of ~14 features — the architecture is aspirational for the bulk of the codebase.
**What will become painful as Sutra grows?**
- Any new feature added to app.js makes the monolith worse and the size floor harder to reduce.
- Any new theme preset requires editing the 35k-line styles.css rather than overriding a small semantic-token surface.
- Any new modal surface must be hand-registered in both contracts.css and app.js.
- Any new LLM provider must be added to the CSP allowlist, the providerMeta registry, the model-capabilities.js capability map, AND the hasAnyProviderConfigured() fallback list — four parallel sources of truth.
- The 26 themes × ~14 views × 4 viewports matrix of visual regressions is not covered by automated screenshot diffing.
- The 427 unsafe DOM sinks ratcheted in the guardrail baseline will compound.
**Does the product feel cohesive?** Yes at the language and visual-identity level. No at the interaction-consistency level. The product's voice is calm and intentional; the product's UI is accumulated rather than designed.
**Which parts feel production-grade?** Sync, persistence, encrypted backup, the assistant safety boundary, the DOM safety layer, the service worker, the release pipeline, the test suite for sync, the cache-stamp lock, the Supabase RLS posture, the verified-wipe instruction verifier. These would not be out of place in a Series-A company's codebase.
**Which parts still feel prototype-grade?** The 85k-line app.js monolith, the styles/legacy/ directory, the parallel token systems, the chaos-persistence.spec.mjs "page rendered" assertions, the source-text-regex contract tests, the property-fuzz.test.mjs deterministic LCG, the 264 inline onclick= handlers, the duplicated navigation taxonomies, the 4 open-signal modal conventions.
**What are the largest risks?**
1. **app.js size floor prevents extraction.** A future maintainer who tries to shrink the monolith will fail CI. The size floor is the wrong shape of guard.
2. **'unsafe-inline' in CSP.** Any XSS-style bug found in the 391 innerHTML sites in app.js runs with full origin privileges and can exfiltrate every stored assistant API key.
3. **Cross-tab race on browsers without Web Locks.** Silent data loss for ~10% of browsers.
4. **verifyDatabasesGone lying on Firefox/Safari.** Advertised security guarantee not delivered.
5. **Credential vault per-profile key decryptable by any same-origin script.** Any XSS exfiltrates all stored credentials.
6. **Two parallel token systems, neither enforced.** Every new theme preset requires editing the 35k-line styles.css.
7. **The 16 AGENTS.md landmines.** Any change to app.js can violate an implicit invariant.
**If another experienced engineer inherited this repository tomorrow, what would concern them most?** The 85,392-line app.js monolith with a CI size floor that prevents reduction. They would open the file, scroll for ten minutes, find that the AGENTS.md :615 admits the file is "large and closure-coupled" with "controllers [that] remain there because they need private helpers," and conclude that the codebase is in a slow-burning maintainability crisis that the existing workflow (core:worktree, core:integrate) does not actually resolve. They would also be concerned by the 427 unsafe DOM sinks ratcheted in the guardrail baseline — the "guardrail" only stops growth, not existence.
**What would impress them most?** The sync subsystem. The encrypted-backup envelope. The action system's transactional model. The DOM safety layer. The persistence pipeline's writeIf + readback verification. The Supabase RLS posture. The verified-wipe instruction verifier. The 12-category envelope tamper matrix. The custom-tabs.js "zero unsafe innerHTML sinks" pattern. The AGENTS.md "Known architectural landmines" document. They would recognize that the team is capable of excellent engineering — and conclude that the consistency debt is a backlog problem, not a capability problem.
---
**GOOD:** Sync subsystem (protocol/engine/merge/crypto/transport/store + Supabase RLS); persistence pipeline (commitAppDataWithHealth with conditional write + readback verification + FIFO queue + detached snapshot); assistant safety boundary (action-system transactional model, wrapUntrusted/defangFence prompt-injection fence, memory classifier with blocked/sensitive tiers); DOM safety layer (allowlist + namespaced user ids + sandboxed iframe rendering + URL scheme re-validation); encrypted-backup envelope (AES-GCM-256 + AAD-bound headers + per-envelope KDF); service worker (reject-on-failure cache.addAll + same-origin-only + network-first navigation + Share Target defensive validation); release pipeline (deny-by-default artifact + verified-deploy SHA artifact + live-smoke); cache-stamp content-hash lock; verified-wipe instruction verifier; custom-tabs.js "zero unsafe innerHTML sinks" pattern; AGENTS.md 16 landmines document; the test suite for sync (sync-engine 806 LOC, sync-merge 571 LOC, sync-crypto 224 LOC, sync-store 294 LOC, sync-schema 184 LOC).
**MID:** Feature-registry pattern governing only 2 features; 8 source-text-regex "contract" tests; property-fuzz.test.mjs deterministic LCG; 26-theme sprawl; centralized modal manager with hand-synced 25-selector list; setTrustedHTML channel relies on developer discipline; notifications.js mixing safe-storage and direct innerHTML; 142 console.warn swallow points (no error boundary); core-runtime-integrity.mjs size floor preventing extraction; two parallel navigation taxonomies.
**BAD:** The 85,392-line app.js monolith with CI size floor (Critical); script-src 'unsafe-inline' (High); cross-tab race without Web Locks (High); verifyDatabasesGone lying on Firefox/Safari (High); credential vault per-profile key with no passphrase prompt (High); background not inert when modals open (High, WCAG); two parallel token systems (High); styles/legacy/ 3,137 lines unpaid debt (Medium-High); legacy-workspace-migration promise that never resolves (Medium); chaos-persistence.spec.mjs no real chaos coverage (Medium); 427-sink guardrail baseline (Medium); HomePage.html separate design system (Medium).
**Biggest strength:** The sync subsystem and the persistence pipeline — genuinely the strongest engineering in the codebase, with real behavior tests, defense-in-depth, and threat-model-aware design (AAD-bound envelopes, security-definer RPCs, anchored-regex RLS, verified-wipe instruction, conflict-storm breaker, deterministic three-way merge, lamport-based dedup).
**Biggest weakness:** The 85,392-line src/core/app.js monolith — the root cause that makes every other weakness harder to fix, compounded by a CI size floor that prevents reduction and an extraction workflow (core:worktree) that adds work without shrinking the monolith.
**Most important next investment:** Begin a real, regression-tested app.js decomposition plan that (a) extracts the already-namespaced bridges (SutraEncryptedBackups, SutraDriveSync, SutraCloudSync) into separate files, (b) shrinks the core-runtime-integrity.mjs size floor as extraction proceeds, (c) is gated by npm run check:runtime + the existing 12-category tamper matrix + the sync-engine test suite. This unblocks every other improvement — including the CSP 'unsafe-inline' removal (which depends on converting 264 inline handlers, which depends on event-delegation patterns that custom-tabs.js already proves work). The decomposition is multi-quarter but each step is independently shippable, and the existing test suite genuinely locks the behavior.
